Run the constitution command engine with the user's arguments passed in a FILE, so no shell ever sees the user's text. Step 1: with your FILE-WRITE tool (not the shell), write the user's arguments, verbatim, on one line, into a new file /tmp/constitution_args_<id>.txt where <id> is a fresh random 12-character [a-z0-9] string (for no arguments write `help`). Step 2: run `bash submodules/constitution/scripts/constitution_cmd/constitution_cmd.sh --args-file /tmp/constitution_args_<id>.txt` (use `bash constitution/scripts/constitution_cmd/constitution_cmd.sh` for the legacy layout, or `bash scripts/constitution_cmd/constitution_cmd.sh` when the constitution is the project root). The engine deletes the file after reading it. The command line contains only that path, never user text. Never put the arguments on a command line, in a heredoc or inside quotes. Subcommands: status, update, doctor, anchors N, gates, report|issue|bug|task|feature, skills, extensions, jev, release-notes, help. With no arguments run `help`. Relay the engine output; never invent status it did not print (section 11.4.6). The engine rejects unknown subcommands (exit 2) and reports a missing delegated tool as unavailable (exit 3) and passes a delegated tool's own exit status through (so 3 can also come from the tool) - relay that honestly, do not work around it.
